signals.title: USD — FOMC Decision + Yield Curve + Positioning
signals.text: The Federal Reserve enters its July 29 decision with the market priced for a hold at 3.75%, yet desk focus remains on a potential hawkish shift as US 10Y yields climb to 4.645%. The yield curve is currently in a bear steepener regime (2s10s at +33.5bp), a combination that typically reinforces USD strength through higher long-term rate attraction. Speculative positioning shows a slight net short of -1,948 contracts (47.2% long), suggesting the market is not yet fully positioned for a hawkish surprise. DXY at 101.45 remains technically supported, trading above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (SMA20 at 101.06). A hawkish hold today likely forces a coverage of those spec shorts and pushes DXY toward the next psychological resistance. Risk: A dovish pivot or emphasis on downside economic risks triggers a sharp USD sell-off toward SMA50.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Positioning + Options + Carry
signals.text: USD/JPY is testing 163.85 ahead of the July 31 BoJ meeting, with a significant +266bp OIS carry advantage (SOFR 3.64% vs TONA 0.98%) sustaining the bid. Despite this carry support, the options market is pricing in heavy downside protection as seen in the 25d Risk Reversal at -1.55, signaling institutional fear of BoJ intervention or a hawkish surprise. CFTC data shows JPY net shorts remain extreme at -114,030 (26.7% long), creating an asymmetric risk profile where any hawkish BoJ shift is likely to trigger a massive short-covering rally in JPY. Price is currently extended above the SMA20/50/200 cluster, with the SMA20 at 162.57 acting as the first major technical floor. Risk: BoJ holds current policy and ignores FX weakness, validating the carry trade and pushing USD/JPY toward 165.00.

signals.title: AUD/USD — ESI Divergence + Volatility + Retail
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6930, pressured by a stark divergence between bullish speculative positioning and deteriorating economic fundamentals. AUD speculative net longs sit at +20,521 (62.8% long), while the Economic Surprise Index (ESI) has plunged to -21.2, reflecting persistent data misses. The options market is pricing in significant tail risk with a +8.5% Vol Risk Premium (IV 14.9% vs HV30 6.4%), the highest in the G10 space. Retail sentiment is currently 61% short, fading the institutional long, which often precedes a flush of the crowded spec position. A break below the SMA200 at 0.6906 would confirm a bearish shift and likely accelerate the liquidation of long positions. Risk: A surprise hawkish hold from the RBA on Aug 11 or a sudden commodities rally invalidates the bearish fundamental read.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Technicals + Oil + Retail Sentiment
signals.text: USD/CAD at 1.4088 is testing the lower bound of its recent range as WTI Oil surges +6.50% intraday to $84.4. The pair's correlation to oil has broken significantly (z = -1.55σ), with the -0.914 correlation suggesting the pair is now hyper-sensitive to energy price swings. Retail sentiment is currently 71% short, which aligns with the heavy spec short position of -99,823 contracts, indicating a lack of contrarian tension and a unified bearish bias toward the pair. Price is currently holding below its SMA20 (1.4122) but remains above the SMA50 (1.4035), creating a tight technical compression zone. Continued oil strength likely forces a test of the 1.4035 level. Risk: An escalation in Middle East sanctions monetization targets, as hinted in recent headlines, is likely to introduce broader USD safe-haven bids that override the oil correlation.
